title: Adaptive Quiet Windows: SLO-driven Surge Escalation and Contextual Runbooks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Noise from transient client spikes and uneven multi-region routing is causing excessive paging during low-impact degradations. Existing on-call pages are generic and require manual context assembly across consoles (trace IDs, region, degraded pipeline stage), slowing MTTR and causing fatigue. We need an SLO-driven, region-aware quiet window and a contextual runbook system that reduces pager volume while enabling rapid, automated triage for real incidents.

Goals: 1) Reduce actionable paging by 45% for alerts classified as "degradation-with-fallback" without increasing P99 user-visible error SLO violations. 2) Provide automated, pre-populated runbooks that include region, model variant, routing tier, recent rollout markers, and KV cache hit-rate in the page payload. 3) Implement a short-term adaptive quiet-window that anneals alert sensitivity during controlled bursts and reopens on capacity/backpressure signals.

Scope: This ticket covers alert routing policy changes, RBAC-safe enrichment hooks for pages, runbook templating and a small orchestration lambda that decides quiet-window activation. It excludes broad circuit-breaker redesign and long-term rollout of cross-region capacity scheduling (tracked separately).

Non-goals: Rewriting the inference router, changing customer visible SLAs, or implementing new on-call rotations.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume for non-customer-impacting degradations reduced by >=45% in measured 30-day window post-rollout
Pages include structured contextual fields: region, model_variant, active_rollout_id, kv_cache_hit_rate_pct, recent_error_rate_1m
Adaptive quiet-window toggles automatically in response to predefined triggers and exposes metric for audits
On-call runbook links open to a pre-filled incident context page with one-click runbook steps and the primary mitigation command
No regressions in P99 latency SLOs attributable to alert suppression in the first 14 days
implementation_steps: Prototype a lightweight decision service (lambda) that ingests alert stream and SLO-meter metrics and returns action: page|suppress|escalate
Add alert enrichment hooks: query region routing table, model variant, rollout id, and recent KV cache hits; attach to page payload via pagerduty/sms headers
Create templated runbook snippets in Confluence with placeholders; implement a small service to render and return the filled URL
Implement quiet-window policy: parameters (duration, sensitivity-scale, cooldown) and signal set (ingress QPS spike, autoscaler lag, queue length, error-rate delta)
Add a non-destructive staging mode to run the decision service in 'audit-only' for 7 days to collect telemetry
Run user testing with 2 on-call volunteers and iterate runbook text and primary mitigation commands
Roll out canary to one non-critical region for 48h, validate metrics, then stagger to remaining regions
Instrument metrics and SLO checks that tie suppressed pages to later customer-impact events for visibility
rollout_plan: Week 0: Deploy decision service in audit-only mode to collect suppression candidates
Week 1: Enable contextual runbook rendering and attach to pages (audit-only deliveries to Slack channel)
Week 2: Enable quiet-window in canary region with auto-fallback disabled and human confirmation required
Week 3: Enable automated quiet-window with immediate fallback triggers enabled, monitor 24/7
Rollback criteria: increase in customer visible SLO violations > 2% absolute or key customer complaints reported
Full roll-out: Gradual activation across regions over 2 weeks once stability confirmed
monitoring_queries: pager_latency_mean: avg(time_to_ack) for pages with runbook_url
post_suppression_slo_violations: count(slo_violations triggered within 30m of suppressed_alert)
quiet_window_activation_count: count(quiet_window_active) by region and reason_tag
risk_mitigation: Start in audit-only mode to detect false-suppression patterns
Keep human-in-loop option for immediate disable of quiet-window per region
Expose suppression audit log to on-call and SRE lead channels
Limit suppression for alerts that indicate complete outages or pager type 'sev0'
Predefine quick rollback playbook that disables decision-service routing and reverts alerting rules

We should reuse existing alert-enrichment library used by incident-telemetry to avoid duplication
